new.statement: Sample efficiency drives the score. An airbench96-style net (frozen 2x2 patch-whitening stem, 3-conv groups at widths 128/384/576, SGD-Nesterov at lr 9 with BN biases at 64x LR, label smoothing 0.3, lookahead-EMA, alternating flip with translate 2) reaches >=75.3% in about 8.5 epochs. The biggest lever on time is cutting the epochs needed to reach the target.

Reproducing the futurebiohackers submission's defaults on this machine (fp16 + channels_last, compile max-autotune warmed up in build on synthetic data, GPU-resident uint8 data, GPU-side augmentation) gives a feasible starting point about 7x faster than the ResNet9 template.

The futurebiohackers defaults (8.5 epochs, bs 1024, last block 576) give a 3-seed mean accuracy >=0.753 and time <=9.0 s on the A100-SXM4, with complete == True. The unmodified ResNet9 template takes >=50 s.
Dirac (identity) init of the 3-conv group convs, which the reference recipe apparently lacks, speeds up early optimization. The airbench paper reports it saves about 1.2 epochs on CIFAR-10.
Adding dirac init and cutting epochs from 8.5 to 7.5 keeps 3-seed accuracy >=0.753 and reduces time by >=8% compared with the A1a reproduction.
Capacity in the last group (7x7/3x3 spatial) is cheap in FLOPs. Widening it lets the epoch count fall by more than the added per-epoch cost.
Last block at 768 with 7.5 epochs gives accuracy >=0.753 and time at least 3% below the 8.5-epoch / 576 reproduction.
Brightness/contrast augmentation, a hiverge CIFAR-10 trick, regularizes CIFAR-100 well enough to allow fewer epochs at equal accuracy.
Adding light brightness/contrast jitter at 8.0 epochs keeps accuracy >=0.753, where the same 8.0-epoch recipe without it falls below 0.753.

Per-epoch compute drives the score. About 95% of GPU time is in conv, BN and activation kernels, so cutting FLOPs or kernel cost per epoch (lower early resolution, a cheaper activation, training on fewer examples) reduces time at constant accuracy.
Progressive resizing (24 -> 28 -> 32 px) makes early epochs much cheaper while costing little final accuracy. Each shape must be compiled and warmed up in build to avoid timed recompiles.
A 24->28->32 px schedule, with at most +0.5 epochs to compensate, cuts time by >=5% compared with the best fixed-32 px recipe while keeping accuracy >=0.753.
GELU is more expensive than SiLU or ReLU under compile/fp16, and swapping it costs no accuracy.
Replacing GELU with SiLU at equal epochs reduces time by >=2% and changes 3-seed accuracy by no more than 0.2 pp.

Training only on high-loss examples, as in Selective Backprop / airbench96_faster, cuts backward compute. With 500 images per class and ~8 epochs, the cost of the proxy or forward pass may outweigh the gain.
After 2 full epochs, backpropagating only the top 60% by loss of each batch (losses taken from the main net's own forward pass) reduces time by >=5% with accuracy >=0.753.

Fixed and per-step overhead is a measurable share of an ~8 s run: timed prepare work (GPU transfer, normalization, whitening eigendecomposition), Python/kernel-launch overhead per optimizer step, and the separate optimizer kernels. Removing it cuts time without touching accuracy.
Compiling the whole train step (forward, backward and a fused optimizer) or capturing it in CUDA graphs removes launch overhead at bs 1024.
A fused/foreach optimizer plus a CUDA-graphed or fully compiled step reduces time by >=2% compared with the reproduction, with accuracy within 0.2 pp.
Prepare (uint8 upload, normalization, whitening init on 5000 images) takes a non-trivial share of timed time and can be shrunk, e.g. fewer whitening images or fused normalization on the GPU.
In the reproduction, prepare is >=3% of prepare+train time. Computing the whitening statistics on 1000-2000 images instead of 5000 cuts prepare by >=30% with accuracy within 0.2 pp.
A larger batch (2000) halves the step count and per-step overhead and raises GPU utilization. LR, wd and momentum need retuning to keep accuracy.
bs 2000 with LR scaled by the kilostep rule, at equal epochs, reduces time by >=3% while keeping accuracy >=0.753.

Accuracy and timing noise set the usable margin. Per-seed accuracy std is about 0.25 pp (3-seed SE about 0.15 pp), so a recipe needs a 3-seed mean around 0.755 or higher to be safe at 0.753 locally and 0.75 over 40 judged seeds. Time differences under about 2% cannot be told apart from noise without a repeat.
Seed-to-seed accuracy variation on the airbench96-style recipe matches the reported ~0.25 pp. Run-to-run time variation for a fixed config is small (CV about 1%) once compile is warmed up in build.
On the reproduction, the per-seed accuracy std over seeds 0-2 is <=0.35 pp. Rerunning the identical config gives a mean accuracy within 0.15 pp and a mean time within 2% of the first run.
Swapping the optimizer (Muon on the conv filters, SGD for biases and head) does not reduce time-to-75% on CIFAR-100, despite its CIFAR-10 gains.
On CIFAR-100, Muon's orthogonalized updates give no sample-efficiency gain over well-tuned high-LR SGD-Nesterov at the airbench96 widths, and the Newton-Schulz steps add per-step cost.
Muon (lr ~0.24, momentum 0.6, 3 NS steps) on the conv filters, at the same epochs as the reproduction, gives accuracy no higher than SGD +0.2 pp and time no lower than SGD -2%.

structured_output.summary:
The tree was empty, so I seeded it with 5 Lvl1 claims, each with Lvl2 mechanisms and numeric Lvl3 predictions. No experiments have run, so no statuses changed. All new items are open.

- **A, sample efficiency (0.75):** an airbench96-style recipe reaches 75.3% in about 8.5 epochs.
  - A1a: reproducing the futurebiohackers submission gives accuracy >=0.753 in <=9 s.
  - Ways to cut epochs: dirac init (A2), a wider last block with fewer epochs (A3), brightness/contrast augmentation (A4).
- **B, per-epoch compute (0.6):** progressive resizing (B1), SiLU instead of GELU (B2), hard-example selection (B3, low prior).
- **C, fixed and per-step overhead (0.5):** compiling the whole train step or using CUDA graphs with a fused optimizer (C1), trimming the timed prepare step (C2), batch size 2000 (C3).
- **D, noise and margin (0.6):** this sets the acceptance rule. Seed std is about 0.25 pp, so a 3-seed mean around 0.755 is needed to be safe. Time gains under 2% need a repeat run (D1a).
- **E, Muon vs SGD (0.6):** a mostly negative claim that Muon is not a win on CIFAR-100.

Recommended first runs:
1. The A1a reproduction. As the reviewer asked, it should also record per-seed accuracy and the prepare/train time split, which tests D1a and C2a.
2. A repeat of the same config, to measure noise.

Every feasible run should also get a standing rule check:
- prepare resets everything learned.
- build touches no real data.
- eval runs in eval mode and stays under 5 s for any batch size from 1 to 1024.
